summary: Four candidates directly apply contrastive learning (representation learning with paired positive and negative examples) to traffic forecasting (predicting road traffic flow). [V0237] (Gupta et al., 2023) applies the method to the MetroFlow dataset, achieving 0.93 accuracy. [V0239] (Adebayo et al., 2025) evaluates on AgriSat-4, reporting AUROC of 0.72. [V0238] (Haddad et al., 2024) uses the Atlas-ICU dataset and reports MAE of 0.65. [V0240] (Brennan et al., 2026) applies the method to LedgerGuard, obtaining F1 of 0.79. These four are the only documents that both (a) use contrastive/paired positive-negative representation learning and (b) directly address road traffic flow prediction. A fifth slot is required; [V0023] (Haddad et al., 2025) applies the same contrastive method but to septic deterioration prediction, not traffic — it is the closest methodological match among remaining candidates but is off-topic. Documents such as [V0197], [V0201], [V0061], and [V0170] only mention contrastive learning for traffic as prior work and do not apply it themselves. Documents using other methods (self-attention, boosted trees, message passing) or other domains are excluded.
